chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Nu'man, the owner of Al-Taqq, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding

a man who caused injury to a slave-girl, meaning his wife, and injured her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the blood-money (diyah) if he had intercourse with her before she reached nine years of age.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he kept her and did not divorce her, there is nothing upon him. And if he had intercourse with her and she was nine years of age, there is nothing upon him; if he wishes, he keeps her, and if he wishes, he divorces her.'

key_terms.افْتَضَّ: to break the hymen; to cause injury to the genitals
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood-money; compensation for injury or death
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: consummated the marriage; had intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyah if a husband injures his wife before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial liability (diyah) for a husband who injures his pre-pubescent wife, establishing that full blood-money is due if she is under nine years old, while no penalty is required if she is nine or older, reflecting the Shia juristic consensus on the age of maturity (bulugh). The ruling highlights the distinction between the right of ownership in the wife's person prior to consummation and the subsequent optionality of retention or divorce without compensation, a nuance central to Shia fiqh of marriage and injury.
